Financial Highlights
•Taxable-equivalent net interest income increased nominally in the recent quarter as compared with the second quarter of 2026 reflecting an additional day, partially offset by lower interest income on nonaccrual loans.
•Average loans grew $2.6 billion in the recent quarter reflecting higher average commercial real estate loan balances of $1.6 billion, consumer loan balances of $634 million and residential real estate loan balances of $367 million.
•Higher noninterest income in the recent quarter reflects an increase in residential mortgage banking revenues, partially offset by a decrease in capital markets and advisory revenues and a lower distribution from M&T's investment in Bayview Lending Group LLC ("BLG").
•Noninterest expense reflects increases in outside data processing and software costs and professional and other services expense as well as higher personnel costs from an additional working day in the recent quarter.
•The allowance for loan losses as a percent of total loans declined 2 basis points to 1.51% at September 30, 2026.
•In the recent quarter, M&T repurchased 1.3 million shares of its common stock at a total cost of $323 million. M&T's CET1 capital ratio is estimated to be 10.16% at September 30, 2026.
Chief Financial Officer Commentary
"M&T's third quarter results were highlighted by strong loan and deposit growth, stable credit and a solid capital position. Fee income in the recent quarter continues to reflect the breadth of M&T's franchise and our ability to meet customers' evolving needs through a wide range of financial capabilities. The continued strength across customer-driven revenue streams demonstrates the value of our diversified business model and the depth of our customer relationships. These relationships are at the heart of our purpose, to make a difference in people's lives. I want to thank our employees for their ongoing commitment to the communities and customers we serve."
- Daryl N. Bible, M&T's Chief Financial Officer

Third Quarter 2026 Results

Financial Reporting Matters
As reported on M&T's Form 8-K dated September 28, 2026, effective for the third quarter of 2026 M&T made certain changes and reclassifications to Other income categories presented in its Consolidated Statement of Income. Also effective for the third quarter of 2026, M&T began separately presenting loans held for sale from loans held for investment in its Consolidated Balance Sheet and its Average Balance Sheet and Annualized Taxable-equivalent Rates disclosures. Accordingly, annualized taxable-equivalent rates for each impacted loan category and certain loan-based credit quality ratios exclude loans held for sale. Additionally, as reported in M&T's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, in conjunction with the implementation of a new general ledger platform during the second quarter of 2026, the Company modified its methodology for calculating annualized taxable-equivalent rates for certain earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, including certain average deposit balances. All periods presented herein reflect those changes.

Third Quarter 2026 Results
Taxable-equivalent net interest income in the recent quarter rose nominally from the second quarter of 2026 reflecting an additional day, lower interest income on nonaccrual loans and loan growth funded by interest-bearing deposits as the Company reduced its average short-term borrowings. Taxable-equivalent net interest income increased $32 million, or 2%, as compared with the year-earlier third quarter reflecting lower rates paid on average interest-bearing deposits and growth in average loans and investment securities, partially offset by lower yields received on loans.

Average earning assets rose $1.5 billion from the second quarter of 2026 reflecting growth in average commercial real estate loan balances of $1.6 billion, average consumer loan balances of $634 million and average residential real estate loan balances of $367 million.
Average earning assets increased $5.8 billion from the third quarter of 2025, reflecting loan growth across all loan portfolios. Average commercial and industrial loan balances increased $4.2 billion, spanning most industry types. Average consumer, residential real estate and commercial real estate loan balances grew $1.3 billion, $1.1 billion and $880 million, respectively. The average balance of investment securities increased $2.0 billion from the year-earlier quarter, reflecting purchases of fixed rate mortgage-backed securities.

3
Third Quarter 2026 Results
Average interest-bearing liabilities in the recent quarter rose $1.9 billion from the second quarter of 2026 reflecting growth in average interest-bearing deposits of $3.5 billion and higher average long-term borrowings resulting from asset securitizations and issuances of senior and subordinated notes. Those increases were partially offset by a $2.9 billion decline in average short-term borrowings from the FHLB of New York.

Average interest-bearing liabilities increased $8.1 billion from the third quarter of 2025 reflecting growth in average interest-bearing deposits of $4.5 billion, higher average short-term borrowings from the FHLB of New York of $1.9 billion and an increase in average long-term borrowings of $1.2 billion resulting from asset securitizations and issuances of subordinated notes, partially offset by net maturities of senior notes.

Effective January 1, 2026, the Company elected to prospectively measure its residential mortgage loan servicing right assets at fair value with changes in fair value reflected in mortgage banking revenues. As a result, amortization associated with residential mortgage loan servicing right assets previously recognized in other costs of operations before 2026 is no longer recorded. Instead, beginning in 2026 fair value changes in residential mortgage loan servicing right assets, inclusive of the realization of expected net servicing revenues over time, are included in mortgage banking revenues. On December 31, 2025, the Company began economically hedging the risk of fair value changes in these assets through the use of various interest rate derivative contracts, for which changes in fair value are also reflected in mortgage banking revenues.

Noninterest income in the third quarter of 2026 increased $3 million from 2026's second quarter.
•Trust and investment services income declined $5 million reflecting seasonal tax services fees earned by the wealth management business in the second quarter of 2026.
•Mortgage banking revenues increased $25 million reflecting a rise in residential mortgage loan sub-servicing income. In June 2026, the Company began sub-servicing $62.9 billion of additional residential mortgage loans.
•Capital markets and advisory revenues decreased $9 million reflecting a decline in loan syndication fees and lower revenues from interest rate swap transactions with commercial customers.
•Other revenues from operations decreased $10 million reflecting a lower distribution from M&T's investment in BLG in the recent quarter.
Noninterest income declined $9 million, or 1%, as compared with the third quarter of 2025.
•Trust and investment services income rose $13 million reflecting higher corporate trust revenues from the Company's institutional services business and an increase in personal trust and investment services revenues from its wealth management businesses.
•Mortgage banking revenues increased $5 million reflecting a rise in residential mortgage loan sub-servicing income, partially offset by the impact of the Company's fair value accounting election described above and lower gains on commercial mortgage loans originated for sale.
•Other revenues from operations decreased $27 million reflecting a $28 million distribution of an earnout payment from the Company's 2023 sale of its Collective Investment Trust ("CIT") business and a $12 million gain on the sale of equipment leases each in the third quarter of 2025, partially offset by an $11 million higher distribution from M&T's investment in BLG in the recent quarter.

Noninterest expense rose $44 million, or 3%, from the second quarter of 2026.
•Salaries and employee benefits expense increased $6 million reflecting an additional working day in the recent quarter, partially offset by lower payroll-related taxes.
•Outside data processing and software costs increased $19 million reflecting higher software maintenance and enhancements to the Company's technology infrastructure.
•Professional and other services rose $8 million reflecting support for enhancements to the Company's technology infrastructure and other enterprise initiatives.
•Other costs of operations increased $6 million reflecting the Company's obligation under agreements to share in losses stemming from certain litigation of Visa, Inc.
Noninterest expense increased $30 million, or 2%, from the third quarter of 2025.
•Outside data processing and software costs rose $35 million reflecting costs associated with enhancements to the Company's technology infrastructure.
•Professional and other services increased $16 million reflecting support for enhancements to the Company's technology infrastructure and other enterprise initiatives and higher legal service costs.
•FDIC assessments were $6 million higher in the recent quarter reflecting the reduction of estimated special assessment expense in the third quarter of 2025 resulting from a decrease in the FDIC's loss estimates associated with certain failed banks.
•Other costs of operations decreased $31 million reflecting the amortization associated with residential mortgage loan servicing right assets in the third quarter of 2025 and lower expense associated with the Company's supplemental executive retirement savings plan in the recent quarter.

Income Taxes
The Company's effective income tax rate was 23.1% in each of the third and second quarters of 2026 compared with 22.8% in the third quarter of 2025.

Total capital13.93 (1)13.73 14.35

(1)Capital ratios at September 30, 2026 are estimated.
M&T's capital ratios remained well above the minimum set forth by regulatory requirements. Cash dividends declared on M&T's common and preferred stock totaled $217 million and $42 million, respectively, for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. M&T's current stress capital buffer is 2.7%.
Reflecting rising interest rates, accumulated other comprehensive income declined $588 million in the recent quarter. In July 2026, the Company transferred $8.3 billion of residential mortgage-backed securities from the available-for-sale portfolio to the held-to-maturity portfolio with net unrealized gains of $8 million. Unrealized losses on those transferred securities at September 30, 2026 were $222 million ($165 million net of tax).
M&T repurchased shares of its common stock at a cost of $323 million during the recent quarter, compared with $465 million and $409 million in the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025, respectively.
The CET1 capital ratio for M&T was estimated at 10.16% as of September 30, 2026. M&T's total risk-weighted assets at September 30, 2026 are estimated to be $170.6 billion. Reflecting loan growth and share repurchase activity in the recent quarter and the impact of unrealized losses on investment securities available for sale included in accumulated other comprehensive income at September 30, 2026, M&T's tangible common equity to tangible asset ratio at September 30, 2026 declined 22 basis points from June 30, 2026 and 94 basis points from September 30, 2025.
While not subject to the liquidity coverage ratio ("LCR") requirements, M&T estimates that its LCR on September 30, 2026 was 107%, exceeding the regulatory minimum standards that would be applicable if it were a Category III institution subject to the Category III reduced LCR requirements.

About M&T
M&T is a financial holding company headquartered in Buffalo, New York. M&T's principal banking subsidiary, M&T Bank, provides banking products and services with a branch and ATM network spanning the eastern U.S. from Maine to Virginia and Washington, D.C. Trust-related services are provided in select markets in the U.S. and abroad by M&T's Wilmington Trust-affiliated companies and by M&T Bank. For more information on M&T Bank, visit www.mtb.com.
